question: Show that $f(x)=-2x+\cos x$ is strictly decreasing on $\mathbb{R}$.
explanation:
Given function
$$f(x)=-2x+\cos x$$
First derivative
$$f'(x)=-2-\sin x$$
Range of sine
For every real $x$,
$$-1\leq\sin x\leq1$$
Hence,
$$-2-\sin x\leq-2-(-1)=-1$$
Sign of the derivative
Thus, $f'(x)\leq-1<0$ for all $x\in\mathbb{R}$. A negative first derivative throughout an interval indicates that the function is strictly decreasing there.
Conclusion
Therefore, $f(x)=-2x+\cos x$ is strictly decreasing on $(-\infty,\infty)$.
